findings.description: @unchecked Sendable on actor is redundant and misleading. Actors are implicitly Sendable in Swift 6. The @unchecked Sendable suggests manual verification needed when actor isolation already provides safety.
findings.remediation: Remove @unchecked Sendable from actor declaration. Actors are implicitly Sendable - no annotation needed.

findings.description: Error? is not Sendable. TranscriptionSegment stores 'error: AudioError?' which may break Swift 6 concurrency checks. Error protocol does not conform to Sendable.
findings.remediation: Create TranscriptionErrorInfo struct: struct TranscriptionErrorInfo: Sendable { let message: String; let code: String; let isRecoverable: Bool }. Convert errors before storage.

findings.description: nonisolated(unsafe) without SAFETY comment. The 'consumed' variable is marked nonisolated(unsafe) but lacks documented justification for why this is thread-safe in the actor context.
findings.remediation: Add SAFETY comment: // SAFETY: 'consumed' is only accessed within the convert closure which is synchronously executed on the actor's thread before the method returns. No cross-actor access occurs.

findings.description: Fire-and-forget Task in actor init creates race condition. Task { @MainActor in self.cachedViewModelFactory = vmFactory } may execute after other init code runs, causing inconsistent state.
findings.remediation: Remove fire-and-forget Task. Make init async or use @MainActor init: @MainActor init(...) { ... cachedViewModelFactory = viewModelFactory }. Consider factory pattern for async initialization.

findings.description: [weak self] in actor-isolated context is unnecessary and potentially problematic. ImportAudioUseCaseImpl is an actor, so closures within its methods already have isolated access. Weak capture could prevent progress updates.
findings.remediation: Remove [weak self] - actors don't need weak capture for internal closures: progressHandler: { progress in self.reportProgress(adjustedProgress) }. The actor's isolation domain ensures proper lifecycle.

findings.description: Defer with async operations is unreliable. The defer block creates a Task for async buffer release, but defer runs when function exits - Task may not complete before process termination or may be cancelled unexpectedly.
findings.remediation: Replace defer with explicit cleanup in do/catch/finally pattern: do { ... } catch { ... } finally { await bufferPool.release(&micBuffer); await bufferPool.release(&sysBuffer) }. Or use withExtendedLifetime pattern.

findings.description: Generic multi-channel path uses scalar loop instead of vDSP. Multi-channel mixing (channelCount > 2) falls back to scalar O(n*m) loop instead of vectorized operations.
findings.remediation: Use vDSP for multi-channel mixing: Create weight vector [1/channelCount] and use vDSP_vsq or vDSP_mmov for parallel channel processing.

findings.description: [weak self] in Task captures within actor may cause premature nil. StreamingSpeechProcessor uses Task { [weak self, chunk] in ... } inside actor - weak capture could cause self to become nil before clearActiveTask() is called.
findings.remediation: Remove [weak self] in actor-isolated Task. The actor's lifecycle manages the task - use Task { [chunk] in ... await self.clearActiveTask() }. Actor deinit will cancel tasks.
